titleEn: No Ground Snow in My Mouth!

pages.text: "Thirsty!" Kiki, the pointy-eared cat, crouched in the alley after a long snowball fight. "Fetching water is a bother..." Kiki scraped together snow from underfoot.
Rolled into a ball, it sparkled like icy candy. "I can eat this!" Kiki lifted it toward the mouth. Nono, the smallest, roundest sparrow, and Gugu hurried over.
Gugu, the broad-chested pigeon, grabbed Kiki's hand. "No, Kiki!" Nono pointed at the footprints. "Everyone walked here." Kiki stopped. "But it is white?"
At the shop, Grandpa Badger filled one bowl with alley snow and another with untouched roof snow. He put both beside the stove.
The snow melted. Alley snow left gray water and black grains. Even the untouched snow left tiny grains at the bottom.
"Every kind of snow has things like these inside. Snow is not for your mouth." Grandpa held up both bowls. Kiki pursed the lips. "No ground snow in my mouth! Ptooey!"
Grandpa poured stove-warmed water into three cups. Kiki drank it all. "Much better than snow!" The thirsty throat relaxed.
Kiki looked up at an icicle. "We cannot eat that either, can we?" "Right. That is frozen snow too." Grandpa nodded. Kiki touched the green bell and stepped back.
Before eating, Kiki remembered three things. "One, do not eat any snow! Two, ask Grandpa! Three, eat only what is served in a bowl!" When Nono reached for snow, Kiki stopped him.
Grandpa sat Kiki on his knee and patted the back. When curious, ask first. Then your tummy will not hurt. Kiki rubbed the tummy. "No ground snow in my mouth! Ptooey!"
